clue.text: Gather berries should be black to go with waffle

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to waffle is to ramble, talk on aimlessly

explanation.surface: Someone muses that foraging for berries pairs nicely with a waffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waffle' looks like breakfast food but is the verb meaning to talk aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To bramble is to go blackberrying, picking fruit from the hedgerow bushes.

clue.text: Midday meal of ancient times, entertaining move by hotel

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means holding them inside

parts.note: BC, before Christ, marks ancient dates
to run is to move quickly
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An ancient meal hosted by a hotel, with movement around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: One of Rome's famous rulers, some around 100

indicators.note: the some word goes around the hundred

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: Rome had perhaps a hundred famous rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some around 100' reads as an approximate count, but 'around' is a container signal, and 100 is the slang ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Antony was one of the Second Triumvirate who governed Rome after Caesar.

clue.text: Lido's inelegant entrances?

parts.note: the entrances are not doorways but ways of entering the water at a swimming pool

explanation.surface: The doorways of a public pool are unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is an open-air public swimming pool; the clumsy entries are into the water, flat on the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A belly flop is a dive landing flat on the stomach with a painful smack.

clue.text: Sign erected left or top right on map

indicators.note: in a down clue erected means built upwards, so read from the bottom

parts.note: north-east is the top right of a map, NE

explanation.surface: A signpost has been put up, pointing left or to the top right of the map.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign on for a course is to enrol, register as a member.

clue.text: Part taken by mascara in Bowie's gay image

indicators.note: a part taken by the words means a run of letters lifted from inside them

explanation.surface: Mascara played its part in David Bowie's flamboyant, androgynous look.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across MASCA-RA IN BOW-IE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow flag is the emblem of the LGBT community, so it is an image symbolising gay pride.

clue.text: Scrap rifles — when loaded often they get worn at the rear

definitions.text: when loaded often they get worn at the rear

parts.note: a ruck is a scrap, a brawl
to rifle a place is to ransack or sack it

explanation.surface: Scrapped rifles, often loaded, are worn at the back by soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifles' looks like guns but is the verb for plundering.
explanation.definitionFit: Rucksacks are packed bags carried on the back by walkers.

clue.text: Giant nest with odd droppings — many have dropped off here

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters keeps the even ones

explanation.surface: A giant nest from which droppings have fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping odd letters of GIANT NEST leaves I, N, N, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are where travellers have slept, nodded off for the night.

clue.text: Weapon whose user shows a lot of cheek

definitions.text: Weapon whose user shows a lot of cheek

parts.words: Weapon whose user shows a lot of cheek
parts.note: the user is not impudent; his cheeks puff out as he blows a dart

explanation.surface: An insolent person armed with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheek' suggests impudence; it is the face puffed out to blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube through which darts are shot by breath.

clue.text: Gush over girl said to be flawless

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the gush above the next piece

parts.note: to well up is to gush out

indicators.note: said to be marks a sound-alike

parts.note: a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses about a girl, calling her perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-made is soundly constructed, without faults.

clue.text: Aunt still stripped off repeatedly, as before

indicators.note: stripping each of the two words removes its outer letters, leaving the insides, done once per word

explanation.surface: An aunt is still undressing, over and over, just as she did before.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Aunt' and 'still' lose their first and last letters, giving UN and TIL.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Wait until dawn' and 'wait before dawn' share the sense of up to a point in time.

clue.text: Two kinds of beach food to eat and unlimited music

indicators.note: the food words take in, as if eating, the next piece

parts.note: seaside rock is the stick of hard candy sold at British beaches, and a roll is a bread roll

indicators.note: without its limits the word and loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A seaside picnic of two foods, followed by music without limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock is the striped sugar stick sold at British seaside resorts; 'to eat' has the two foods swallowing the middle letter of 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock 'n' roll is the 1950s popular music style built on guitar and a heavy beat.

clue.text: Daughter getting into fancy cooking, losing sugary stuff

indicators.note: the daughter's letter gets into the middle of the other letters
something being cooked is being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
a losing is taken as a loss

explanation.surface: A daughter takes up elaborate cookery but abandons the sugary treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges the letters of 'fancy' to CANYF, and 'getting into' puts the daughter's D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Candyfloss is spun sugar on a stick, the fairground treat Americans call cotton candy.

clue.text: A cutting politician's flipped over — this writing's unwelcome

indicators.note: flipped over means the result is read backwards
A cuts into the politician's letters, sitting between them

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament, so MPS with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A politician has done a U-turn, and his writing is not wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts A inside MPS to give MAPS; 'flipped over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is junk email, unsolicited messages that nobody wants to receive.

clue.text: Bad reaction of a grouser agitated about parking Sierra

indicators.note: letters agitated about are shaken around into a new order

parts.note: P is the sign for parking
S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A complainer gets worked up over parking in Sierra.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour grapes is resentful disparagement of something one failed to get, from Aesop's fox.

clue.text: How one may come out on top after taking a short cut

definitions.text: How one may come out on top after taking a short cut

parts.words: How one may come out on top after taking a short cut
parts.note: the top is the head, and a short cut is a haircut, so this is how one's hair looks after a trim

explanation.surface: Someone wins through by taking a quicker route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out on top' suggests winning and 'short cut' a quick route; both refer to hair on the head after a very short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-cropped describes hair trimmed very short to the scalp.

clue.text: Small sides in vessel

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
sides in sport are teams
in means fashionable, as does hip

explanation.surface: Little teams squeezed into a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is a word for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a seagoing boat driven by steam engines.

clue.text: Maybe diamond and pearls set to be worn by king and queen

indicators.note: the jewels and the king are combined, the king inside the rearranged pearls
pearls set in jewellery are arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Jewellery of diamond and pearls is set for royalty to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges the jewels' letters to SPARLE, and 'to be worn by' loosely mingles the king's K into them; the queen follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkler is slang for a diamond or other glittering gem.

clue.text: Sailor's hand-made joint rocks offshore wader

parts.note: a reef is a ridge of rock just offshore
the knot is a wading shorebird

explanation.surface: A sailor's handmade joint wrecks a wading bird on the offshore rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot is the square knot tied by hand by sailors to join two ropes.

clue.text: See papers united on Keeping Up Appearances

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, to see
the press is the newspapers collectively
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
RE means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Look: the newspapers all agree about the sitcom Keeping Up Appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping Up Appearances is a British TV sitcom about a snobbish social climber; here the phrase means conforming to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer pressure is the social push to match what friends and neighbours do.

clue.text: Play with no opening, play with no ending — extremely radical show

indicators.note: having no opening means the first letter goes

parts.note: fun is play, amusement

indicators.note: having no ending means the last letter goes

parts.note: fun is play, amusement

indicators.note: the extreme letters of the word are its first and last

explanation.surface: A review of two flawed plays and an extremely radical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like drama but is fun; UN, FU and RL are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfurl a flag or banner is to show it, spreading it open.

clue.text: Charlie, installed in a post, gets rise

indicators.note: installing puts the letter inside the others

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie is given a job and earns a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go up, climb.

clue.text: General is mellow, getting loud not soft

indicators.note: in music notation f is loud and p soft, so one letter swaps for the other

parts.note: ripe fruit or cheese is mellow

explanation.surface: A senior officer has mellowed, though he is now shouting rather than whispering.
explanation.walkthrough: In music p (piano) means soft and f (forte) means loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Rife and general both describe something widespread, found everywhere.

clue.text: Newcomers crushed miming star

indicators.note: something crushed is pulped out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: New arrivals trampled a mime artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Immigrants are people newly arrived to settle in a country.

clue.text: Writer of one's bio turned up with nothing missing, twice

indicators.note: missing tells us the letters for nothing are taken away
in a down clue turned up means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as written; the reversed letters do contain the writer, but the clue gets there by removing the two O's ('with nothing missing, twice'), not by a hiding signal, so the overlap is a coincidence of construction

indicators.note: twice means the letter for nothing is used two times

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A writer's biography published with nothing left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives OIBSENO from ONE'S BIO; 'missing' removes both O's.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House.

clue.text: Article definitely in German, third from Merkel not being totally open

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
ja is German for yes, definitely

indicators.note: third from a word means its third letter

explanation.surface: A German article from Angela Merkel was definitely not fully candid.
explanation.walkthrough: Angela Merkel was Chancellor of Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A door ajar is slightly open, not fully opened.

clue.text: Yearns to own Beatle's old clothing?

indicators.note: the yearning word owns, holding inside, the Beatle

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn for it
John Lennon was a Beatle; the 's makes him the thing owned

explanation.surface: A fan longs to possess a Beatle's vintage clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Long johns are old-fashioned full-length woollen underwear.

clue.text: Take a break every year and exercise

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year
to exercise a right or skill is to use it

explanation.surface: Advice to have a holiday each year and keep fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause is to stop briefly, resting before carrying on.

clue.text: Nasty corner pop-art target covers over

indicators.note: over tells us the hidden letters are read backwards
the words cover the answer, holding it within their letters

explanation.surface: A pop-art target painting is draped over, perhaps hiding something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pop-art target' backwards (TEGRAT TRA POP) and the answer is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattrap is figuratively a bad spot that is hard to escape, a tight corner.

clue.text: Ruled roost previously — became cuddly

indicators.note: the roost comes previously, before the ruling word

parts.note: a bird's roost is its nest
to lead is to rule, so ruled is led

explanation.surface: A bird ruled the roost in the past, then went soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to snuggle close, so nestled means snuggled up affectionately.
